newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla soars as P&G denies Norway plans.
newsitem.headline: Orkla soars as P&G denies Norway plans.

text.p: Shares in food and beverage conglomerate Orkla ASA jumped on Thursday in heavy trade after U.S. consumer products giant Procter & Gamble denied a Norwegian media report that it would imminently move into the Norwegian detergents market.
At 1356 GMT Orkla's A share was up 20 crowns, or nearly four percent at 548 crowns. The B share was 15 crowns higher at 495 crowns.
Daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv reported this week that Proctor & Gamble was planning to set up shop in Norway and that Orkla is bracing itself for a tough fight on its home turf.
Orkla's A stock tumbled 25 crowns on Tuesday to 548 crowns and an additional 20 crowns on Wednesday following the report.

"Proctor & Gamble have no immediate plans to launch detergents in Norway right now. I don't know where the rumours originate from, but they didn't come from us," Jeanette Ehrnrooth, spokeswoman for the U.S. firm told Reuters.
The report had added to poor sentiment in the market following Orkla's disappointing four-month results last Thursday, which led to a 14 percent plunge in Orkla A shares up until Wednesday's close.
